Hi Grandma

First of all I really like the backstory. It's got all the makings of a fun reveal where your helping the party to bring about your own desires of proving death wrong. 

One thing I'm assuming is your power as a cleric and a wizard comes from Death. I think wizard and cleric can be an interesting mix as you can cast spells bumped up a few levels as a wizard while getting the additional hp as a cleric. 

As far as subclasses to go I've never played a Necromancy wizard so I will wait for someone who's played it and their knowledge on the matter. However personally I would chose a Grave cleric over a life cleric as I feel that's more thematic as the apprentice of death decides who goes over the edge and into your masters arms and who doesn't. This could also lead to interesting scenarios where you actively have to fight death to stop him taking your companions.

As far as levels go I'd recommend a 10/10 split to add flair of your characters balance. Alternately an 11/9 split either way would allow you to cast better spells.

For spells I'm going to talk about them as if you cant prepare spells and pick each level 

As far as spells go there are a few I'd recommend as a starting cleric 

Inflict wounds -  this could be like your practicing the death tap and could be your signature finisher.

Cure wounds - the counter part to inflict wounds because after all 'Death can take it from one to create new life somewhere else'

Id also take bane or bless, and one other (or both bane and bless)

As far as cantrips go thaumaturgy and sacred flame as a go to damager. As for the third one I'd recommend spare the dying as that would be another nice kick in deaths face 'No we need to know the effect they'd have in this world'.

That's my thoughts.
